source_ref: Zhan, N. (2024) 'Factor structure, measurement invariance, and psychometric properties of the Posttraumatic Cognitions Inventory (PTCI) and its brief version (PTCI-9) in Chinese adolescents and adults', Psychological Assessment 36(4):291-302, doi:10.1037/pas0001309. MAPPING: the study's own OSF deposit https://osf.io/tj8rh/ -- README.txt (https://osf.io/download/4bt7v/, 1416 bytes), which states the ptci1..ptci33 renumbering of the original 36-item form, and data/PTCI_data.sav (osfstorage 65800c29513a741d80aed38f, 174822 bytes), whose ptci* variable labels give each renamed column's subscale plus a 'b-' flag for the PTCI-9 items. TEXT: Foa, E.B., Ehlers, A., Clark, D.M., Tolin, D.F. & Orsillo, S.M. (1999) 'The Posttraumatic Cognitions Inventory (PTCI): Development and validation', Psychological Assessment 11(3):303-314, Appendix A (items, instructions, 1-7 anchors) and Appendix B (subscale key), PDF as posted by two of the co-authors' own centre at https://oxcadatresources.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Foaetal.PTCI_.PsychAssess.1999-1.pdf. PTCI-9 item set (original numbers 1,7,22,23,25,27,31,33,36) per Wells et al., Assessment 26(2):193-208, doi:10.1177/1073191116685401. Processing script data/ptcichina_zhan_2024.R. Cached under itemtext/.cache/ptcichina_zhan_2024/.
note: MAPPING (paper_explicit, two explicit numbered links, no order inference): data/ptcichina_zhan_2024.R keeps the .sav column names verbatim (select(starts_with("ptci")) then pivot_longer), so item IS the source column name -- core model s3 pattern 1. Those columns are a RENUMBERING of the original PTCI, and the deposit's README.txt states it line by line: originals 1-12 keep their numbers, 14..31 -> 13..30, 33 -> 31, 35 -> 32, 36 -> 33, with originals 13, 32 and 34 dropped because Foa (1999) Appendix B marks them experimental and excludes them from every subscale. Item wording is then read off Foa (1999) Appendix A by original number. README TYPO, resolved not guessed: its line 32 reads 'ptci35 -> ptci21', but ptci21 is already the target of line 21 ('ptci22 -> ptci21') and ptci32 is the only unclaimed target, so 35 -> 32; every README line is also numbered with its own new code, and that ordinal reads 32. CORROBORATION (Step 5b, PARTIAL): PTCI_data.sav labels each renamed column with its subscale and prefixes 'b-' on the nine PTCI-9 items -- labels written against the RENAMED codes and independent of the README. Predicting each shipped sentence's class from Foa Appendix B plus the published PTCI-9 set (originals 1,7,22,23,25,27,31,33,36) reproduces all 33 labels exactly (self=18, world=4, blame=2, b-self=3, b-world=3, b-blame=3); see verify_ptcichina_zhan_2024.R, VERDICT: PASS. This pins class, not position within a class, so status is PARTIAL. STEP 3b CLEAN: 33 live items on a 1-7 scale is exactly the PTCI's 33 scored items and its 7-point agree/disagree metric; nothing else in the study (LEC-17, PCL-20, PHQ, GAD, SWLS) has that shape. LANGUAGE / FALLBACK: administered in Chinese, and no Chinese wording is recoverable within scope -- PTCI_data.sav has zero real CJK (only binary noise under a gb18030 read) and no value labels on any ptci* column; PTCI_retest.sav's strings are ASCII variable names only; the OSF r-script and mplus-syntax folders and PTCI_only_data.dat carry none; the Mendeley companion deposit (data.mendeley.com/datasets/3f8hh825b5/1) holds the same PTCI_data.sav plus analysis zips; the APA article itself is paywalled and lists no open supplement. So this is the translated_substitute fallback: English in the base fields, language=Chinese, no _translated columns, translation_source=official_instrument_english (Foa et al.'s own English for the same numbered items, NOT a translation of the administered Chinese, which may have diverged in the Chinese adaptation). DEVIATIONS from literal transcription, all from the same PDF-text defect: the Appendix A text layer drops the leading 'I' from originals 20, 21, 23, 24, 25 (it sits in the number column) and renders anchors 2 and 7 as '1'. Restored to the canonical readings -- 'I have permanently changed for the worse.' (a trailing comma in the text layer restored to a period), 'I feel like an object, not like a person.', 'I can't rely on other people.', 'I feel isolated and set apart from others.', 'I have no future.', and anchors 2='Disagree very much', 7='Totally agree'. Nothing else was normalised; the ID/INITIALS/DATE header line was dropped from instructions as form furniture. OPTION AXIS: not inferred -- Appendix A prints the numbers beside the anchors, ascending 1=Totally disagree .. 7=Totally agree, and the live resp set is exactly 1-7. RIGHTS: no block. No clause reserving a right in the PTCI wording is locatable, so under the 2026-09-08 test silence is permission. The only copyright notice inside Foa (1999) other than APA's own article notice is on FIGURE 1 -- 'From Treating the Trauma of Rape (p. 84), by E. B. Foa and B. O. Rothbaum, 1998, New York: Guilford Press. Copyright 1998 by Guilford Press. Reprinted with permission.' -- which governs a schematic diagram, not Appendix A; the APA article notice is an article notice, the PANAS case. Two of the five co-authors' own centre (OxCADAT, Oxford) posts the full-text PDF including both appendices for open download with no stated terms. No fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term was found on any of those, and instrument_rights_register.csv has no PTCI row. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION of both the renumbering and the restored pronouns: a third-party 33-item PTCI handout (https://goodmedicine.org.uk/media/files/ptsd,%20assessment,%20ptci.pdf, 2pp) prints the same 33 statements in the same renumbered order -- its 13 is original 14, its 33 is original 36 -- and lists its subscales in RENUMBERED terms as self 2,3,4,5,6,9,12,13,15,16,19,20,23,24,25,27,28,29,31,32,33 / world 7,8,10,11,17,22,26 / blame 1,14,18,21,30, identical to the assignment shipped here. It also carries the leading 'I' on its items 19, 20, 22, 23, 24 (originals 20, 21, 23, 24, 25) and the anchors 1=totally disagree .. 7=totally agree, confirming both PDF-text repairs. It is not the transcription source -- it lowercases and unpunctuates -- so wording still comes from Foa (1999) Appendix A.
public_note: The PTCI was administered to this Chinese sample, but neither the OSF deposit nor the paywalled article publishes the Chinese wording, so item_text here is the instrument's original English (Foa et al., 1999, Appendix A) rather than what respondents read; a Chinese adaptation may differ from it. Item codes are also a renumbering, not the original PTCI numbering -- ptci13 onward are shifted because originals 13, 32 and 34 (the experimental items excluded from every subscale) are absent, so ptci13 is original item 14 and ptci33 is original item 36.

ITEM TEXT: the instrument author's own distribution of the English original -- SD3.1.1 - 27 items, https://www2.psych.ubc.ca/~dpaulhus/Paulhus_measures/SD3.1.1.doc, sha256 17779ba2195c32705970d28d6a7f962a0df683422f01224405596b1fb53cdb2e, fetched 2026-09-10, dated May 2014 (Jones, D. N., & Paulhus, D. L. (2014), 'Introducing the Short Dark Triad (SD3)', Assessment 21:28-41). ADMINISTERED INSTRUMENT: Zhang, J., Ziegler, M., & Paulhus, D. L. (2020), 'Development and evaluation of the short Dark Triad - Chinese version (SD3-C)', Current Psychology 39:1161-1171, doi:10.1007/s12144-019-00272-3. IRW PROCESSING SCRIPT: data/qi_2025_self_reported_scales.R.
note: PASS WITH CAVEATS (batch_146, 2026-09-10). 135 rows, 27 items x 5 response levels; validate_items.R --table-sets passes both sets (27 items, resp 1-5) and irw-validate is clean; per-item n is a uniform 134 across all 27 items. STEP 3b (INSTRUMENT MATCH). The table is the Short Dark Triad, not the Dirty Dozen: the live data has 27 items on a 1-5 scale, which is the SD3's shape (the Dirty Dozen is 12 items), and the source paper says 'The dark triad were measured by the short Dark Triad-Chinese version. This scale comprises three subscales that assess Machiavellianism, narcissism, and psychopathy, each consisting of 9 items ... a five-point Likert scale, anchored by 1 (completely disagree), and 5 (completely agree).' The workbook's Names_of_variables sheet lists DT = The dark triad with exactly those three subdimensions in that order. SOURCE / WHY NOT data_labels. The deposit's Scales.xlsx carries NO item wording at either level: the Summary_of_data header row is bare codes (DT_1..DT_27) and the Names_of_variables sheet gives only scale and subscale names, not items. The paper's Supplementary materials docx (41_2025_6035_MOESM1_ESM.docx, 8 tables) documents the ten experimental tasks' stimuli only and contains no questionnaire text. So the words come from the instrument, not the study. LANGUAGE FALLBACK (text_source=translated_substitute). The administration was Chinese (SD3-C). The administered Chinese wording is in neither the deposit nor the paper's supplement -- the two places recoverability is scoped to -- so the base text fields carry the SD3's English original as distributed by Delroy Paulhus himself (SD3.1.1.doc), language=Chinese, and no _translated columns are emitted. translation_source=official_instrument_english: this is the instrument publisher's own English for the same numbered items, a parallel version rather than a translation of the administered Chinese string, so where Zhang et al.'s adaptation diverges in wording this will not correspond word for word. MAPPING (paper_order, Step 5b PARTIAL). The IRW code IS the source column name (core model s3 pattern 1 -- data/qi_2025_self_reported_scales.R takes items = paste0('DT_', 1:27) straight off the workbook header, no positional step), but the source column name carries no text, so pattern 1's exemption buys nothing here and no exemption was claimed. The tie from DT_n to a specific SD3 item is inferred from the instrument's own presentation order (Machiavellianism 1-9 = DT_1..DT_9, Narcissism = DT_10..DT_18, Psychopathy = DT_19..DT_27). That inference was tested against the paper's published per-subscale Cronbach's alphas for this exact sample (.71 / .75 / .64) and reproduced them to within .003 (.712 / .748 / .637) -- alpha depends on both block membership and the reversal set, and the five SD3 reverse items landing anywhere other than DT_11, DT_15, DT_17, DT_20, DT_25 breaks it (narcissism unreversed = .135; psychopathy unreversed = .750, DT_25 only = .771, DT_20 only = .604). Re-runnable as verify_qi_2025_dark_triad.R (VERDICT: PASS). What it does NOT establish: the order of the non-reversed items WITHIN a block -- swapping the text of DT_2 and DT_3 would not move any number here -- hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. REVERSE CODING IS NOT APPLIED IN THE TABLE. The processing script states 'Do not reverse-score any items', and the raw item-rest correlations confirm it: DT_11 -0.31, DT_15 -0.08, DT_17 -0.23 against a positive rest of the narcissism block, and DT_25 -0.10 in psychopathy. DT_20 ('I avoid dangerous situations', reverse-keyed) is the one apparent anomaly -- it reads +0.42 raw and has a low mean (1.81) -- but it is genuinely the reverse item: including its reversal is exactly what takes psychopathy alpha from .771 down to the published .637, i.e. the authors reversed it too and it is simply a weak item in this sample. No polarity was changed in the shipped text. TRANSCRIPTION DEVIATIONS. (1) The '(R)' reverse-scoring markers that SD3.1.1 prints after five items are scoring annotations, not administered wording, and were stripped. (2) Everything else is byte-for-byte from the doc, including its inconsistent apostrophes (item DT_1 has a straight quote, DT_5/DT_7/DT_22/DT_23/DT_27 typographic ones) and the missing full stop on DT_26. (3) option_text is SD3.1.1's own five anchors (Strongly Disagree / Disagree / Neither Agree nor Disagree / Agree / Strongly Agree); the paper glosses only the two endpoints, and in different words ('completely disagree' / 'completely agree'), so one register was used throughout rather than splicing two -- the middle three anchors have no study-side gloss at all. instructions is SD3.1.1's own one sentence. Single trivial section_id, blank section_prompt (no testlet or shared-passage structure); correct_response blank (an attitude scale, no key). RIGHTS. Not a block, and no clause reserving a right was locatable. Delroy Paulhus's measures page (https://www2.psych.ubc.ca/~dpaulhus/Paulhus_measures/, sha256 af5a0308c83e2a1a42aa5b327f8e4b97487d4250feb2cf5dd527bbba6c9a0854, fetched 2026-09-10) splits his instruments into 'In the Public Domain -- The following questionnaires are available without permission. Feel free to download and use as needed.' and 'Limited-Use Questionnaires -- The following questionnaires are available for research use. Permission of the author is required.' The SD3 appears on NEITHER list; its successor the Short Dark Tetrad (SD4) is on the public-domain one, and the limited-use list (BIDR-6, UBC Word test, SRP, OCT) does not include it. The SD3.1.1.doc the author serves from that same directory carries no fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause of any kind -- only scoring instructions, norms and citations. Under the 2026-09-05 test (irw#1945) silence is permission, so this ships. public_note: Respondents completed the Chinese adaptation of the Short Dark Triad (SD3-C; Zhang, Ziegler & Paulhus, 2020), but the administered Chinese wording appears in neither the study's OSF deposit nor its supplementary materials, so IRW ships the SD3's English original as distributed by its author (SD3.1.1, May 2014) with language recorded as Chinese -- a parallel version of the same numbered items rather than a translation of what respondents read, so wording the Chinese adaptation changed will not correspond word for word. The 1-5 anchors are the English instrument's (Strongly Disagree ... Strongly Agree); the paper labels only the endpoints, as 'completely disagree' and 'completely agree'. Responses are stored raw: the five reverse-keyed items (DT_11, DT_15, DT_17, DT_20, DT_25) have not been reverse-scored, which reproduces the paper's published subscale alphas of .71/.75/.64 to within .003.
